claims.text: Replacing part of the ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr in AlCoFeNi will increase coercive field.
The coercivity increase will result from a two-phase hierarchical microstructure that provides domain-wall pinning sites.
AlCoFeNi annealed at 1000 °C for 15 hours forms a single ordered B2 phase.
AlCoFeNi annealed at 1000 °C has a coercivity of approximately 4.3 Oe.
The intervention is to replace approximately 50% of Co with Cr, producing AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi.
Arc melting followed by annealing at 600 °C for 15 hours can induce phase separation in the investigated alloys.
The Cr-substituted alloy will form a B2 matrix containing fine to nanometer-scale BCC precipitates and clusters.
Cr substitution induces B2 plus BCC phase separation in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi.
Cr is antiferromagnetic relative to the ferromagnetic Co it replaces.
Phase separation is caused by positive mixing enthalpies between Cr and the ferromagnetic elements.
The refined secondary phases increase coercivity by acting as domain-wall pinning sites.
The local reduction in saturation magnetization caused by Cr contributes causally to increased coercivity.
Coercivity is predicted to rise from approximately 4 Oe in Cr-free AlCoFeNi to approximately 39 Oe or higher in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi.
A Cr-free AlCoFeNi baseline annealed under conditions similar to the proposed 600 °C treatment will remain a homogeneous single B2 phase.
Annealing temperature can modify the hierarchical phase structure and coercivity.
Cr substitution may create a trade-off between increased coercivity and reduced saturation magnetization.
Failure of the Cr-substituted alloy to reach at least twice the baseline coercivity would falsify the hypothesis.
Absence of the expected hierarchical precipitate microstructure in the Cr-substituted alloy would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The homogeneous single-B2, approximately 4.3 Oe baseline is specifically established at 1000 °C, whereas the matched experiment anneals both alloys at 600 °C and nevertheless expects the baseline to remain homogeneous. The cited record states that Cr-free AlCoFeNi annealed at 600 °C decomposes into B2 plus fine BCC precipitates and has Hc = 14.5 Oe, so the proposed 600 °C baseline is not the stated 4.3 Oe single-phase baseline.
